heading: What the game is
snippet: Grump the Baby Destroyer  is a browser-based 3D survival-horror game. You play a baby left behind in an empty school. Runs entirely in the browser — no build step, no backend, no install — and multiplayer is peer-to-peer

heading: The design rule
snippet: There is no correct answer. Every option costs resentment — some less than others, but never zero — and refusing to talk to him at all costs the most of all:  +6 resentment at the following nightfall  if you never spoke

heading: How a question is picked
snippet: When you talk to Grump, the game first works out his current tier from his resentment total, then picks a random question from that tier that you haven't been asked yet this run (falling back to any question at or below

heading: Every question, in order of tier
snippet: Cost is shown as resentment added if you pick that answer.

heading: Calm (resentment 0–21)
snippet:
Hallo. Are you having a nice last day? 
  −6  “Yes! Very nice!”  Nice. Everyone had a nice one. I asked you about YOURS.  
  −5  “Not really.”  Then you should have gone home. Like the others did.  
  −8  “...”  Silence.

heading: Uneasy (22–49)
snippet:
Why did they all get picked up and you did not? 
  −6  “They forgot me.”  Nobody forgets. They decide, and then they call it forgetting.  
  −8  “I do not know.”  You do know. You are just not saying it out loud yet.

heading: Cold (50–74)
snippet:
The little ones. Are you keeping them from me? 
  −10  “They are just safe with me.”  Safe. There is that word again.  
  −12  “No.”  I counted them yesterday. I count very well.  
  −9  “Yes.”  At last. Something true.

heading: Hostile (75+)
snippet:
How many nights do you think you get? 
  −14  “As many as I need.”  Need. Listen to it. NEED.  
  −12  “I do not know.”  I do. I have the number. I am not telling you the number.  
  −16  “Enough to get out.”  Out. There

heading: What is never shown
snippet:
Bob never appears on the map, at any time, under any circumstances.  You have no way to see him coming except your own eyes and ears.

heading: Rooms lit on the map
snippet: While the generator is running, every currently-lit non-hallway room is tinted faintly amber on the map, so you can tell at a glance which rooms Bob has already switched off behind him.

heading: Day 1 — the fixed list
snippet: The list is always the same three jobs:  Get the lights working ,  Lunch time ,  Round them up . A fuel can and a spare part are pre-placed near the boiler-room generator specifically so day 1 always has a guaranteed way

heading: Night 1 — learning Bob
snippet: Bob is active from night 1 on every difficulty, at his slowest patrol/chase speeds of the run. Get to your classroom, keep the lights on, and treat any hum or torch beam as a reason to go quiet. If he spots you, running

heading: Days 2–3 — the Big Boys Club, and building a buffer
snippet: Somewhere in one of these two days (50/50 which), three big kids corner you in a hallway — a scripted cutscene you can't avoid or fail. Just let it play; it costs you nothing and actually lowers Grump's resentment by 20.

heading: Day 4 — he turns
snippet: Grump stops asking questions and starts hunting, in daylight as well as at night, no later than today — regardless of how carefully you've played. If your resentment management has been bad, this can happen earlier; it c

heading: Nights 5+ — modifiers begin
snippet: From night 5, every night rolls one twist (two from night 10) — Storm, Overtime, Hungry, the Long Night, He Is Closer, or Cold Night. Read the toast at the start of the night; it tells you exactly which modifier(s) are a

heading: Night 7 — the last required night
snippet: Survive it the same way as every other night: light, distance, hiding when it's actually safer than running. The morning after, the front doors' chains come off.

heading: Day 8 — the doors are open
snippet: Walk to the front doors and hold  E  for 2 seconds to leave and end the run as a win (everyone still alive shares the escape in co-op). Or keep playing past the required nights for more score — the run only continues get

heading: What to actually do, day one
snippet: Day 1's job list never changes: get the generator started, eat something, and carry one toddler to your classroom. A fuel can and spare part are already sitting near the generator in the boiler room specifically so you c

heading: Watch the clock
snippet: The top bar shows the phase and time remaining. With 30 seconds left in the day, a banner warns  "IT IS GETTING DARK"  — that's your cue to be heading toward your classroom, not still across the map.

heading: Surviving your first night
snippet:
Get to your classroom and keep the lights on.  A lit room (brightness above 0.55) is the one place Bob won't touch you, and the one thing Grump can't enter before he's turned. 
    Bob is the only real danger for your fi

heading: Talking to Grump
snippet: If Grump approaches and wants to talk, just pick any answer — there's no correct one, every option costs him a little patience, but ignoring him entirely for a whole day costs more (+6 resentment at nightfall) than answe

heading: Easy things to forget, early on
snippet:
Eat.  Your tummy drains constantly; below 25% you get a warning, and at 0% you start losing health. 
    Clean messes you walk past  — it's the only in-play action that calms Grump down, and it stops the generator burnin

heading: Once you've survived a night or two
snippet: Move on to the full  Walkthrough  for a complete run, and  Tips & Strategy  for deeper optimisation once the basics feel automatic.

heading: Tips & Strategy
snippet:
Tips & Strategy 
 Every tip here follows directly from a mechanic documented elsewhere on this wiki — see the linked pages for the underlying numbers. 

 Keep the generator boring

heading: Keep the generator boring
snippet: Repair before you refuel.  Condition below 30% risks a random stall at any moment, and wear itself adds up to 0.12/s to the burn rate — a generator at 50% condition burns noticeably faster than one at 100%, on top of eve

heading: Beating Bob
snippet: A lit room is a full stop, but only if you're not already caught.  He gives up chasing the instant you reach one (unless he's standing right next to you) — so knowing where the nearest lit room is matters more than pure

heading: Managing Grump
snippet:
Say something, anything, every day.  Not talking to him at all costs +6 resentment at nightfall — more than most single answers. There is no way to avoid paying him some attention. 
    Clean messes specifically to calm

heading: Jerry and Meredith
snippet:
Don't fight Jerry's chase.  Hiding cancels him instantly and costs you nothing — there's no reason to let him corner you if a hiding spot is closer than he is. 
    A passed gym class is a real buffer, not just points.

heading: Getting the most out of searching
snippet:
Spread your searches across containers rather than hammering one.  A fresh container's first search is always the full loot table; a second search on the same one is already down to 45% odds of finding anything.

heading: General survival
snippet:
Eat before you're desperate.  Below 20% food you move slower, and below 15% your fear rises faster too — hunger compounds every other problem at once. 
    A teddy is a fear-management item, not just a toy.  Holding one

snippet:
Room codes are five letters, generated by  PeerJS  when the host opens a room. A few things to check: 
 
   The  host's tab must stay open  the whole time — the host machine is running the actual simulation, not a server

heading: Why do my searches keep coming up empty?
snippet: This is by design and gets more noticeable the longer a run goes: the odds of a container actually holding something drop every night, hitting their leanest around night 8 and staying there. See  Loot Tables  for the exa

heading: Grump turned before day 4 — is that a bug?
snippet: No. Pushing his resentment to 100 through rude answers, ignoring him, or leaving messes uncleaned brings his turn forward; being polite never delays it past day 4. Day 4 is a hard ceiling, not a fixed trigger point — see

heading: I can't find Bob on the map
snippet: That's intentional — Bob is never shown on the map, at any time, in any circumstance. See  The Map .

heading: I lost the game / it crashed — is progress saved?
